title: Parable of the Lost Sheep
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child narrates Luke 15:1-7: Pharisees grumble that Jesus eats with sinners, a shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to find the one lost sheep, carries it home on his shoulders and calls friends to rejoice; there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parable of the lost coin.
floor.question: What did the woman do when she found the coin?

representations: a hundred dots with one apart
steps: A shepherd loses one of a hundred.
He leaves the ninety-nine and searches.
He carries it home and rejoices: so does heaven.
contexts: herders in Maasai land looking for a lost goat
a classmate who has stopped coming to church

board.do: Draw ninety-nine dots together and one far away.
Point at the one far away.
board.say: What did the shepherd do about this one?

board.do: Wait for the child to say he left the ninety-nine to find it.

listen_for: He said one sheep was not worth looking for
misconceptions.ask: What did the shepherd do when one sheep was lost?
How did the shepherd bring the sheep home?

listen_for: There is no joy in heaven over a sinner
misconceptions.ask: What did Jesus say in Luke 15:7?

listen_for: To teach farmers how to keep sheep
misconceptions.ask: Why did Jesus tell the parable of the lost sheep (Luke 15:1-2)?
misconceptions.repair: Read Luke 15:1-2 first and ask: who is the lost sheep in real life?

checks.question: What did the shepherd do when one sheep was lost?
checks.answer: Left the ninety-nine and searched for it

checks.question: What makes heaven rejoice, according to Luke 15:7?
